JNJ.rationale: JNJ presents a mixed but slightly positive picture. Fundamentally, the company is a wide-moat healthcare leader with strong franchises in oncology (Darzalex) and immunology (Tremfya), a AAA balance sheet, and a 64-year dividend increase streak. TTM revenue of ~$93.7B and net income of ~$26.9B confirm durable earnings power. However, trajectory is mixed: Q1 2026 showed solid revenue of $24.1B (beat) and raised guidance to $100.8B midpoint, but the Stelara patent cliff is a real headwind (sales down 59% YoY per the Q1 report), and the Q1 2025 EPS of $4.54 was inflated by a one-time item, making sequential comparisons noisy. Operating cash flow was weak at $2.51B in the latest quarter vs. $9.17B prior, though this may be seasonal. On valuation, the stock trades at a P/E of 26.7x — near the top of its 365-day range (16.3–26.8) and well above the ~17x level from a year ago, despite only modest earnings growth. P/B of 6.9x is also near the top of its 4.5–7.6 range. This rich valuation relative to own history limits upside. The near-term catalyst is the Q1 beat-and-raise (April 14, 2026), which is positive but appears largely priced in given the stock's run from ~$146 to ~$230 over the past year. Talc litigation remains an unresolved overhang with 67,000+ plaintiffs. Net: solid defensive franchise, but stretched valuation and patent-cliff headwinds keep the score modest.

Strong pipeline: Icotyde early launch (~1,500 Rxs), Tremfya growing rapidly, Darzalex $4B quarterly sales
